newsitem.title: USA: Boston Edison to sell generating plants.
newsitem.headline: Boston Edison to sell generating plants.

text.p: Boston Edison Co said on Wednesday that it would sell its gas- and oil-fueled generating plants to reduce the company's stranded costs.
The utility said the divestiture plan is a result of an agreement between Massachusetts Attorney General Scott Harshbarger, the state's Division of Energy Resources and Boston Edison.
The plan precedes deregulation of the electric utility industry in Massachusetts, which is scheduled to begin January 1, 1998.
"We anticipate that the new owners of our generating stations could be among the nation's or the world's major power generating companies," said Boston Edison President Thomas May.
Boston Edison also said it will continue to own and operate its Pilgrim Station nuclear power plant in Plymouth.
